preamble: Loss of the voiced labiodental fricative [v], usually between vowels, where the weak labial friction disappears. Middle English lost [v], the voiced allophone of Old English f, in words like head (heved > hed) and lord (loverd > lord).

examples.from: Middle English heved (< Old English hēafod 'head')
examples.note: Old English intervocalic f was voiced [v]; the [v] was lost in Middle English (variants heved, hed).

examples.from: Middle English loverd, laford (< Old English hlāford 'lord')
examples.note: The intervocalic consonant of loverd was dropped.
